text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. Developers regularly add their code to a shared repository, and automated builds start immediately. As part of these builds, the system runs tests to check that everything works correctly. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become serious problems. CI pipelines organise these steps into a clear process, from building the code to running tests and reporting results. Because problems are found quickly, developers can fix them sooner, which saves time and reduces stress. In short, CI makes software development faster, safer, and more reliable for everyone involved.
